episode.title: Keep session state available under SQLite contention and reconcile incomplete transcript migration
episode.before: At parent commit 3a7907b278169110d4fe16e1d50cb316ad5944e0, SQLite connections waited 10 seconds for locks; duplicate session creation used a strict INSERT; an initialization failure discarded the agent's database handle for its remaining lifetime; message flushes assumed the parent session row already existed; message search held one lock while performing every context query; and transcript loading returned any non-empty SQLite result without checking whether legacy JSONL contained a longer history.
episode.after: At b81d49dc450a56791a4ba39401f785eaff573d59, connections wait 30 seconds, session creation is first-write-wins and idempotent, transient initialization failure no longer disables the database handle, every flush idempotently ensures the session row before appending messages, search context queries use separate short lock acquisitions, and transcript loading reads both SQLite and JSONL then chooses the longer source, preferring SQLite on equal counts.
episode.diff: The commit modifies gateway/session.py, hermes_state.py, and run_agent.py and adds regression coverage in tests/gateway/test_session.py and tests/test_hermes_state.py. The implementation changes strict session insertion to INSERT OR IGNORE, adds ensure_session and invokes it at the flush boundary, preserves the database object after create_session errors, increases the SQLite busy timeout, narrows search lock scope, and replaces SQLite-first early return with length-based reconciliation of dual transcript stores. The targeted added test classes execute successfully: 10 tests passed.

evidence_units.claim: Commit b81d49dc450a56791a4ba39401f785eaff573d59 is the implementation-bearing resolution for PR/issue 3249 and has parent 3a7907b278169110d4fe16e1d50cb316ad5944e0.
evidence_units.source: issue-bundle.json fields resolved_commit, parent_commit, linked_pull_requests; git show --format=fuller b81d49dc450a56791a4ba39401f785eaff573d59

evidence_units.claim: The resolution changes three implementation files and two test files, with 247 insertions and 33 deletions.
The parent connected to SQLite with timeout=10.0, while the resolved implementation uses timeout=30.0 to allow a concurrent WAL writer more time to finish.
Session creation changes from strict INSERT to INSERT OR IGNORE, making repeated creation of the same session identifier non-throwing and preserving the first row.
A new ensure_session operation inserts a minimal session row with INSERT OR IGNORE and commits it, without overwriting an existing row.
The message-flush boundary now calls ensure_session with the active session identifier, source, and model before calculating the append range and writing messages.

When initial create_session raises, the agent logs the error but no longer assigns None to its database handle, leaving later flush and search operations able to recover after transient contention clears.
evidence_units.source: git diff 3a7907b278169110d4fe16e1d50cb316ad5944e0 b81d49dc450a56791a4ba39401f785eaff573d59 -- run_agent.py; AIAgent initialization

evidence_units.claim: Message search now releases the lock after the primary FTS query and independently locks each surrounding-context query instead of holding one lock across all sequential context queries.
Transcript loading now reads both SQLite and legacy JSONL, returns JSONL only when it contains more messages, and otherwise returns SQLite, including the equal-length case.
Gateway resume, retry, compression, session-switch, and related paths consume SessionStore.load_transcript, so source reconciliation controls the conversation history restored into those flows.
evidence_units.source: git show b81d49dc450a56791a4ba39401f785eaff573d59:gateway/run.py; load_transcript call sites at lines 550, 2005, 2980, 3015, 3779, 3953, and 3983 in the pinned tree

evidence_units.claim: Regression tests prove duplicate create_session calls do not raise and retain the first row, ensure_session creates a missing row, ensure_session does not overwrite an existing row, and a message can be appended after late session-row creation.
A regression test inspects SessionDB initialization and requires the configured SQLite timeout to contain the new 30-second value.
Transcript regression tests cover JSONL longer than SQLite, SQLite longer than JSONL, empty SQLite with populated JSONL, both sources empty, and equal lengths preferring SQLite.
The two added regression test classes passed at the pinned implementation: 10 passed in 1.11 seconds.
evidence_units.source: uv run --with pytest pytest -o addopts='' -q tests/gateway/test_session.py::TestLoadTranscriptPreferLongerSource tests/test_hermes_state.py::TestConcurrentWriteSafety in a git archive of b81d49dc450a56791a4ba39401f785eaff573d59

evidence_units.claim: In the parent, any non-empty SQLite transcript caused an immediate return, so a partially populated migrated database could hide a longer legacy JSONL history.
In the parent, create_session failure permanently set the agent database handle to None, and the flush path appended messages without first repairing a missing session row.

candidate_atomics.name: make-session-row-creation-idempotent
candidate_atomics.title: Make session-row creation safe to repeat
candidate_atomics.description: Use first-write-wins insertion for stable session identifiers so concurrent components or restarts can request the same parent row without raising or overwriting established metadata.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent duplicate session identifiers from turning normal concurrent or restart behavior into a persistence failure.
semantic_action.pre_state: Creating an already-present session identifier executes a strict insert and can raise an integrity error.
semantic_action.post_state: Creating the same identifier repeatedly succeeds, leaves one session row, and retains the metadata from the first successful creation.
semantic_action.validation: Create the same identifier twice with different metadata and verify no exception occurs and the stored row still contains the first write.

candidate_atomics.name: repair-missing-session-parent-before-flush
candidate_atomics.title: Repair a missing session parent before appending messages
candidate_atomics.description: At the persistence boundary, idempotently establish the minimal parent record required by message foreign keys before appending new conversation rows.

semantic_action.intent: Allow later persistence to recover when initial session registration failed transiently.
semantic_action.pre_state: The database handle is usable but the active session row may be absent, so appending child messages can violate the parent-row requirement.
semantic_action.post_state: A minimal parent session row exists before message appends, while any pre-existing row remains unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Verify missing-row creation, existing-row no-op behavior, and successful message append after late parent creation.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-persistence-capability-after-transient-init-failure
candidate_atomics.title: Keep persistence available after transient initialization failure
candidate_atomics.description: Retain the initialized storage object when initial session registration fails so later flushes and searches can retry after contention clears.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent a transient startup error from disabling persistent session features for the entire agent lifetime.
semantic_action.pre_state: An exception during initial session-row creation causes the live database handle to be discarded.
semantic_action.post_state: The database handle remains available after registration failure, allowing later operations to recover through normal persistence boundaries.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the exception path to confirm it reports failure without clearing the handle, then validate the downstream flush repair operation independently.

candidate_atomics.name: bound-sqlite-contention-wait
candidate_atomics.title: Give concurrent writers a bounded recovery window
candidate_atomics.description: Increase the connection-level busy timeout so short-lived write ownership by another process can clear before an operation fails.

semantic_action.intent: Reduce avoidable lock failures during concurrent writes without introducing unbounded waiting.
semantic_action.pre_state: The connection abandons lock acquisition after a window shown by the change to be too short for observed batch flush contention.
semantic_action.post_state: Lock acquisition waits for the configured longer finite interval before reporting failure.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect or instrument connection construction and assert the configured timeout is at least the selected contention window.

candidate_atomics.name: shorten-search-lock-critical-sections
candidate_atomics.title: Release the database lock between search context queries
candidate_atomics.description: Separate the primary search query from per-result context lookups so a result set does not monopolize the shared connection lock across multiple round trips.

semantic_action.intent: Allow other threads to interleave database work while search results are enriched with context.
semantic_action.pre_state: One lock acquisition covers the primary query and every sequential context lookup for all matches.
semantic_action.post_state: The primary query completes under one lock, and each context lookup uses its own bounded lock acquisition.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the lock boundaries and exercise search to verify matches still receive context or an empty context on lookup failure.

candidate_atomics.name: select-most-complete-transcript-source
candidate_atomics.title: Restore history from the most complete transcript source
candidate_atomics.description: Load every available representation of a session and select by message count, with the richer primary representation winning ties.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent an incomplete migrated store from silently truncating restored conversation history.
semantic_action.pre_state: A non-empty primary store is accepted immediately even when a legacy store contains substantially more history.
semantic_action.post_state: The source with more messages supplies the restored history; equal counts select the primary store; absent or empty sources produce the available history or an empty list.
semantic_action.validation: Test both ordering directions, primary-empty fallback, both-empty behavior, and equal-length tie-breaking with distinguishable message contents.

candidate_workflows.name: recover-session-persistence-after-sqlite-contention
candidate_workflows.title: Recover session persistence after transient database contention
candidate_workflows.description: Harden session creation and flush behavior so concurrent writers or duplicate registration do not permanently disable searchable, foreign-key-consistent session state.

workflow_graph.goal: Keep session storage usable and structurally consistent when startup registration encounters transient locks or duplicate identifiers.
when_to_use: Multiple processes or threads share an embedded session database and startup or flush operations can overlap.
A failed initial parent-row insert currently disables later persistence or leaves child-message writes unable to satisfy their parent relationship.
Search enrichment performs multiple database round trips while sharing the same connection lock.
anti_goals: Do not remove foreign-key enforcement or append orphaned messages.
Do not overwrite established session metadata during recovery.
Do not retry forever or conceal persistent storage failures.
Do not change message ordering or the existing flush cursor semantics.
not_applicable_when: The storage engine has no lock contention, uniqueness constraint, or parent-child session/message relationship.
The database object itself is invalid or permanently unavailable rather than temporarily contended.
Session identifiers are intentionally unique per registration attempt and duplicate creation represents data corruption.
workflow_graph.entry_state: Initial registration may collide with another writer or duplicate identifier; a transient exception can leave the session row absent even though the database becomes usable later.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The database capability remains live, repeated parent creation is harmless, every message flush establishes its parent row first, lock waiting is finite but tolerant of short contention, and search enrichment no longer holds one lock across all context queries.

steps.condition: Use when observed writer batches can outlast the prior connection timeout.
steps.validation: Confirm connection construction uses the selected finite timeout and the timeout regression test passes.

steps.condition: Use when the same stable session identifier can be registered by a restart or concurrent component.
steps.validation: Create the same session twice and verify the first row survives without an exception.

steps.condition: Apply to initialization errors after a usable database object has already been constructed.
steps.validation: Verify the failure handler retains the database handle for downstream operations.

steps.condition: Run before appending messages whenever initial parent creation may not have completed.
steps.validation: Verify a missing parent is created, an existing parent is unchanged, and a child message can then be appended.

steps.condition: Apply when search enrichment performs one context lookup per match on a shared locked connection.
steps.validation: Verify primary results and context enrichment remain correct while lock acquisition is scoped per query.

validation_ladder: Statically verify finite timeout configuration, first-write-wins insertion, retained database lifecycle, pre-append parent repair, and reduced search lock scope.
Run unit tests for duplicate parent creation, missing-parent repair, no-overwrite behavior, post-repair child append, and timeout configuration.
Exercise a real two-writer workload to confirm transient contention clears without permanent feature loss; this integration check was not present in the inspected change.
stop_conditions: Stop if the database handle cannot be safely reused after the reported exception.
Stop if idempotent insertion would hide conflicting identifiers that must be rejected by the domain.
Stop if parent repair cannot preserve existing authoritative metadata.
Stop and investigate if contention consistently exceeds the bounded wait, indicating a persistent transaction or deadlock rather than a transient collision.
unresolved_or_deferred: No added test directly injects create_session failure into AIAgent and asserts that the handle remains live through a later flush.
No concurrent multi-process stress test directly measures the 30-second timeout or reduced search lock scope.

candidate_workflows.name: prevent-transcript-truncation-during-store-migration
candidate_workflows.title: Prevent transcript truncation while two persistent stores coexist
candidate_workflows.description: Reconcile primary and legacy transcript representations at read time so a partially populated migrated store cannot eclipse a more complete conversation history.

workflow_graph.goal: Restore the most complete available conversation history during a transition where old and new transcript stores may contain different prefixes or lengths.
when_to_use: A session can predate the current persistent store and continue writing during migration.
The new store may contain only recent messages while the legacy store still contains the full older history.
Consumers currently stop at the first non-empty source and exhibit abrupt history truncation.
anti_goals: Do not concatenate both sources blindly and create duplicate messages.
Do not delete or rewrite the legacy source as part of read reconciliation.
Do not prefer legacy data when both sources have equal completeness and the primary source carries richer fields.
Do not claim that message count proves semantic equivalence or correct ordering between divergent equal-length histories.
not_applicable_when: Only one transcript source exists and partial migration cannot occur.
The stores contain disjoint shards that must be merged rather than alternative representations of one ordered transcript.
Completeness is defined by sequence numbers or version metadata that is more authoritative than message count.
inputs: messages from the primary transcript store
messages from the legacy transcript store
workflow_graph.entry_state: The primary store may be non-empty but contain only a recent suffix, while the legacy store contains a longer history that the old early-return policy ignores.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The loader returns the longer available transcript, returns the available source when the other is empty, returns empty when both are empty, and deterministically prefers the richer primary representation on equal counts.

steps.condition: Apply when both stores represent the same session but migration can leave their populations at different lengths.
steps.validation: Use distinguishable fixtures to prove both longer-source branches, empty-source behavior, both-empty behavior, and the equal-length primary tie-break.

validation_ladder: Construct fixtures where each source independently has more messages and assert that the longer transcript is returned.
Verify empty-primary fallback, both-empty output, and equal-length tie-breaking.

Resume a legacy long-running session across two post-migration turns and confirm the model-visible and subsequently saved history does not shrink; this end-to-end check was not included in the inspected tests.
stop_conditions: Stop if the two sources do not represent the same logical session.
Stop if message count is not a valid completeness proxy for the storage formats.
Stop if either source cannot be read safely without destructive migration.
Stop and require a stronger reconciliation key when equal-length stores can diverge and field richness does not establish authority.
unresolved_or_deferred: The change does not compare message identities, timestamps, or sequence prefixes; it uses message count as the completeness proxy.
The tests validate source selection directly but do not execute a full multi-turn gateway migration scenario.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub evidence bundle lacks the PR body, reviews, status checks, issue body, comments, and timeline, so intent beyond the commit message and implementation cannot be independently corroborated from discussion.
The implementation provides no direct concurrent multi-process stress oracle for actual lock contention duration.
The transcript policy assumes the longer source is the more complete representation and does not detect equal-length divergence.
The search lock-scope change has no newly added dedicated concurrency or interleaving test.
